title: REPA-G: Test-Time Conditioning with Representation-Aligned Visual Features
claim: Class labels and text prompts give coarse or verbose control; conditioning on visual features yields precise, compositional generation.
layout: 2 columns: left prior conditions, right ours; feature arrows flow to outputs
description: The figure is split by a vertical line. The left column shows baselines in two rows. The top row is labeled 'Class Condition ⟨Angora Rabbit⟩' and shows a fluffy white rabbit. The bottom row is labeled 'Text Prompt', with a long paragraph describing a white albino rabbit on volcanic terrain next to a stylized, painterly rabbit-on-lava image. The right column shows the feature-based method. In the top row, an anchor rabbit photo goes to a colorful patch-feature map ('Image Feats.'). An arrow labeled 'Avg.' leads to an orange square, then to a generated rabbit on a rug. In the bottom row, a masked feature map of the rabbit and a lava photo with a small yellow box, which yields a turquoise square, both lead to a rabbit sitting on glowing lava. The eye goes first to the large photographic images and the colored squares.
caption: Comparing class-label, text-prompt, and REPA-G conditioning. All models are trained on ImageNet. (Top) We average extracted features ( ) from a anchor image to generate a generic “rabbit” image. (Bottom) We combine a masked feature map with a specific “lava” patch ( ) to synthesize a rabbit on a volcano. While text prompts require lengthy descriptions and often lack precision, our feature-based conditioning offers better compositional control and provides more precise generation.
abstract: While representation alignment with self-supervised models has been shown to improve diffusion model training, its potential for enhancing inference-time conditioning remains largely unexplored. We introduce Representation-Aligned Guidance (REPA-G), a framework that leverages these aligned representations, with rich semantic properties, to enable test-time conditioning from features, in generation. By optimizing a similarity objective (the potential) at inference, we steer the denoising process toward a conditioned representation extracted from a pre-trained feature extractor. Our method provides versatile control at multiple levels of granularity, ranging from patch level matching via single patches to broad semantic guidance using global image feature tokens. We further extend this to multi-concept composition, allowing for the faithful combination of distinct concepts. REPA-G operates entirely at inference time with no additional training required, offering a flexible and precise alternative to often ambiguous text prompts or coarse class labels. Our approach achieves high-quality, diverse generations on ImageNet and COCO. Code is available at https://github.com/valeoai/REPA-G
